extracted.intended_audience: IP practitioners (patent attorneys and agents), law firm partners, corporate IP department managers, and others interested in IP practice economics
extracted.subtask_description: A set of survey-defined economic, workload, billing, and demographic metrics used to characterize IP professionals (by practice type and years of experience). The page reports medians/means, quartiles, and breakdowns (billing methods, time allocation, output) for use in benchmarking and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gross income (average, median, expected)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported average and median total gross income for respondents (e.g., "The average 2022 gross income...", median 2022 year-end values, and expected gross income for 2023). Data sometimes reported for full-time only and earlier reports may have included part-time respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons across years should account for changes in inclusion (e.g., prior reports included all respondents vs. current full-time only). Both average and median are provided and broken out by practice type and years of IP experience; charts show quartiles (1st quartile, median, mean, 3rd quartile).

rubrics_metrics.name: Billable hours (median and average)
rubrics_metrics.description: Median and average number of billable hours recorded in the year (e.g., "The median number of billable hours recorded in 2022 was 750" for solo practitioners; medians by practice type/years of experience are reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported with quartile summaries (1st quartile, median, mean, 3rd quartile) and compared across survey years; declines or increases are interpreted in context (e.g., COVID-19 effects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hourly billing rate (median and average)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported median and average hourly billing rates for respondents (e.g., "The hourly 2022 billing rate averaged $439 for solo practitioners, while the median was $400").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented by practice type and years of experience, with quartile statistics. Use caution comparing across years if sample composition changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distributional statistics (1st quartile, median, mean, 3rd quartile)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey uses quartiles and means to display distributions for gross income, billable hours, billing rates, and dollar amounts billed (charts label 1st quartile, median, mean, 3rd quartile).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quartile presentation allows examination of spread and skew; consult both median and mean to understand central tendency especially when distribution is skewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent time allocation to IP work types
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of respondents' time spent on categories such as IP prosecution work, IP litigation, managing outside counsel for IP prosecution, office management/administration, business development, and non-IP legal work (e.g., "Solo practitioners spent an average of 47.3% of their time on IP prosecution work").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breakdowns are reported by practice type and compared with prior surveys. Individual subareas (patents, trademarks, general IP) are reported as percentages of total time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent time spent by IP area (patents/trademarks/etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentages of time devoted specifically to patents, trademarks, general IP work, etc. (e.g., "More than half (55.2%) of responding solo practitioners’ time is typically spent on patents").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported by practice type and compared across years; useful for benchmarking role focus (prosecution vs. litigation vs. transactional).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of new priority US and PCT patent applications prepared and filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Average and median counts of new priority US and PCT patent applications prepared and filed in the year (e.g., "average of 11.1" for solo practitioners; values reported by practice type and years of experience).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as average and median; compare across practice types and across survey years to track workload/output trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dollar amount billed for legal services (median and average)
rubrics_metrics.description: Median and average total dollar amount billed for legal services performed in the year by respondents (e.g., "The median dollar amount billed for legal services in 2022 by responding solo practitioners was $240,000").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented by practice type and years of experience with quartiles. Useful for revenue benchmarking; note whether figures include only legal fees (excludes copy/drawing/government fees where indicated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Billing method breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage breakdown of how services were billed (hourly, predetermined fee, discounted hourly rate) (e.g., "In 2022, an average of 58.7% of solo practitioners’ services were billed on an hourly basis. Another 40.5% were billed using a predetermined fee. An average of 17.5%... billed at a discounted hourly rate").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported by practice type; percentages may sum to more than 100% if respondents bill different matters by different methods. Useful for understanding pricing models across practice types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Year-end cash bonus (median and average)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported median and average year-end cash bonuses for respondents (e.g., "The reported median 2022 year-end cash bonus for solo practitioners is $17,800, with an average of $23,300").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bonus data may be reported for all respondents regardless of employment status; compare medians and means and across years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer contributions to retirement/savings plans (401(k)/403(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Average and median employer contributions to respondents' retirement and savings plans (e.g., "Employer 2022 contributions... averaged $30,798, median $18,000").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sometimes reported for all respondents (full-time and part-time); use caution when comparing to prior years if sampling differs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographic and background characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent demographics and background including age, years of IP attorney experience, years of IP non-attorney experience, highest level of education (excluding law degree), and major field of academic study (e.g., electrical engineering, biology/biotechnology), and self-reported gender and race/ethnicity percentages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These characteristics are used to stratify other metrics (income, billable hours, billing rate). Reported averages/percentages are compared to prior survey waves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing/organizational metrics (direct/indirect reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts or categories indicating number of direct or indirect IP lawyers and patent agents reporting to respondents (e.g., "47.7% ... reported that they did not have any direct or indirect IP lawyer and patent agent reports").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported for corporate IP department heads and attorneys; useful for understanding management responsibilities and correlating with compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time spent on office management/administration and business development
rubrics_metrics.description: Minutes/hours or percent of time spent on non-billable tasks such as office management and administration and weekly hours on business development (e.g., "Office management and administration is reported this year to take up an average of 9.6% of the responding solo practitioners’ time"; "private firm, equity partners reported spending an average of 5.6 hours per week on business development").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as percent of time or hours per week; helps benchmark non-billable workload expectations by role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical charges for IP law services (service-level median fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Median charges for 63 specified IP law services, grouped under six headings (Trademarks [12 services], US Utility Patents including foreign-origin patents where no substantive direction is received [26 services], US Utility Patents of Foreign Origin where foreign attorneys provide substantive direction [10 services], Filing US Applications Abroad [Europe/EPO] [7 services], Other US Patents and Copyrights [6 services], and Transactional Work [2 services]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charges are to be reported only by respondents personally responsible for representative work, based on cases with no unusual complications, and include legal services only (exclude copy, drawing, or government fees). Medians are provided by year for trend comparison (2008–2022 where available).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes on data comparability and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Contextual reporting notes such as whether income figures are full-time only or include part-time, and statements interpreting trends (e.g., the decrease in median gross income from 2020 to 2022 likely due to decreased billable hours and COVID-19 effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should read footnotes and methodological notes: sample composition changes, whether data from firm and individual surveys were combined for particular items, and confidentiality protections that suppress data for small cell sizes (ISD).
